title: Soft version retirement with graceful regional routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a soft retirement and regional routing policy for version-pinned models so customers experience minimal disruption when a pinned model version is deprecated or unavailable in a region. This ticket covers policy matrix, runtime decision logic, rollout mechanics, observability, and migration nudges for customers.
narrative: Background: Customers can pin model versions for compatibility and reproducibility. When a pinned version is deprecated, patched, or temporarily unavailable in a region (capacity/AMI mismatch/quantization mismatch), we need an automated, observable, and reversible mechanism to route traffic to safe alternatives while honoring customer preferences where possible.

Goal: Implement a "soft-version-retirement" flow that (a) attempts transparent routing to the most compatible variant in the same region, (b) falls back to a regional peer only when allowed by customer policy, (c) surfaces an explicit deprecation runway and migration guidance in the Console and API responses, and (d) provides operators with rollback controls.

Non-goal: This ticket does not change global pinning contracts (customers can still opt into strict pinning). It also does not replace the full deprecation notification system — it plugs into the existing deprecation signals.
Owner: Runtime routing team; collaboration with Console and Customer Success for UX and communication templates.
design_notes: Policy matrix: three levels of customer preference: STRICT_PIN, SOFT_PIN, UNPIN_ALLOWED. Default is SOFT_PIN for newly onboarded models unless customer explicitly selects STRICT_PIN.

Decision graph at inference time (ordered): 1) is pinned version healthy in-region? -> serve; 2) compatible variant in-region? -> route to in-region variant with version-compatibility shim; 3) if policy allows regional failover and a peer region has healthy copy -> route to peer region with latency and data residency annotation; 4) if none available and policy == SOFT_PIN -> attempt degraded mode (lower sequence length cap / reduced parallelism) on nearest variant; 5) if STRICT_PIN -> return explicit error with migration guidance.

Compatibility scoring: use a lightweight integer score (0-100) computed from architecture match, quantization level, tokenizer parity, and perf profile. Only variants with score >= 70 are considered automatic substitutes.

Deprecation runway: when a version is scheduled for retirement, mark states: ANNOUNCED -> RESTRICTED_ROUTES -> READ_ONLY -> RETIRED. During ANNOUNCED window (30 days default), SOFT_PIN customers receive automated migration suggestions; during RESTRICTED_ROUTES (14 days) automatic cross-region routing may start for SOFT_PIN; STRICT_PIN gets explicit opt-in to be migrated by Customer Success.

Circuit-breaker: add per-customer adaptive circuit-breaker for cross-region routing that steps down if p99 latency increases by >30% for 3 consecutive 1h windows, with auto-revert after stability checks.

Audit/logging: every routing decision must emit a RouteDecision event with fields: request_id, customer_id, original_pin, chosen_variant, reason_code, compatibility_score, latency_estimate. These are stored in the request-trace stream and surfaced in Console per-route traces.

Trade-offs: aggressive automatic migration reduces downtime but increases risk of subtle behavioral drift; we mitigate with compatibility thresholds, canary-percent routing, and user-visible diff examples in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements the ordered decision graph and honors customer pin policy (STRICT_PIN|SOFT_PIN|UNPIN_ALLOWED) for model selection.
Compatibility scoring computed and used in decision path; threshold configurable via runtime config (default 70).
RouteDecision events emitted for all cross-variant/regional redirections and visible in Console traces within 5 minutes of the request.
Deprecation state machine implemented and integrated with existing deprecation signals; Console displays runway banners and a migration checklist for affected customers.

Automated tests and chaos tests cover: regional unavailability, variant incompatibility, and circuit-breaker triggers; manual QA verifies migration UX in Console and API error messages for STRICT_PIN customers.
Rollback flag and kill-switch available to operations to disable automatic regional routing per-customer and globally.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (feature-flagged deploy): Deploy decision logic behind runtime feature flag; add RouteDecision event schema and Console trace consumer. Limited to internal customers and 2 pilot customers.
Phase 1 (pilot): Enable for 5% of SOFT_PIN traffic for low-risk models in region us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Monitor metrics for 48h windows and iterate on thresholds.
Phase 2 (expanded pilot): Add 25% of SOFT_PIN traffic and enable cross-region peering to one sibling region. Run stability checks and adjust circuit-breaker sensitivity.

Phase 3 (customer opt-in): Expose SOFT_PIN toggle in Console with clear migration checklist and preview of sample diffs. Allow customers to opt their pinned routes into automatic soft-retirement handling.
Phase 4 (default): Flip default for new models to SOFT_PIN and make automatic routing the default behavior for eligible customers unless they explicitly choose STRICT_PIN.
test_plan: Unit tests for compatibility scoring and decision graph permutations.
Integration tests that simulate: region outage, model binary mismatch, tokenizer mismatch, and quantization mismatch.
Chaos tests using the capacity simulator to induce partial regional failures and validate circuit-breaker and auto-revert behavior.
Load tests to ensure RouteDecision emission does not add >2% CPU overhead in the runtime path.
End-to-end QA with one pilot customer: confirm Console banners, per-route trace visibility, and migration recommendation accuracy.
Post-deploy smoke: scripted scenarios to flip into RETIRED state and verify error messages for STRICT_PIN customers.
metrics_to_monitor: p50/p90/p99 latency for pinned routes (by customer and region)
percent of requests subjected to cross-variant routing
RouteDecision event rate and top reason_codes
customer-visible error rate for STRICT_PIN when version unavailable
circuit-breaker open rate and auto-revert events
Migration adoption rate (number of pins converted to newer versions within runway window)
implementation_notes: API change: add optional 'pin_policy' field to ModelPin object with enum {STRICT_PIN, SOFT_PIN, UNPIN_ALLOWED}; default if omitted is SOFT_PIN for new pins.

Console: add per-pin banner with deprecation runway, 'Start migration' CTA that creates a guided checklist and invokes a dry-run that returns a small set of example outputs comparing old vs candidate variant.
Runtime: lightweight compatibility adapter layer for tokenization differences; adapter can be disabled per-model to prioritize fidelity over availability.
Ops: add a 'regional-routing' toggle in Ops Console and a per-customer override list; ensure audit entries for overrides.
